text:
IncidentBot: ALERT: Elevated tail latency and streaming stalls detected on /v1/stream endpoints. p95 jumped from ~420ms -> 1.1s, p99 from ~2.5s -> ~6.2s; increased 5xxs observed. Detected at 2026-03-15T08:02:00Z.

Maria (oncall): ack. looking. assigning Jun. tagging runtime team.

Jun (sre): I'm seeing a correlated spike in cache miss rate on prefix-cache namespace A. Miss rate went from 8% -> 62% after the 08:00 deploy we pushed. KV fetch latency also increased (med 3ms -> 22ms).

Zach (runtime): that deploy was the prefix-hash rekey rollout (v2). We changed the salt/hash ordering to improve distribution. possible namespace mismatch?

Priya (eng-ml): any change to model variants or tokenization around 08:00? we didn't touch model code, only routing + prefix hashing for cache keys.

Jun (sre): logs snippet:```[2026-03-15T08:01:58Z] cache_lookup namespace=A key=pf-0x7f miss
[2026-03-15T08:02:01Z] kv_fetch latency=18ms key=pf-0x7f
[2026-03-15T08:02:05Z] stream stall request_id=abc123 stall_ms=2200
```

Leo (prod-ops): observed a rapid drop in hit-rate on that namespace + immediate p99 spike in streaming. hypothesis: prefix hash change invalidated cached prefixes, causing cold miss storm + kv backend pressure -> request queuing -> streaming tail stalls.

SRE-bot: Suggested playbooks: prefix-cache rollback, cohort throttles, route high-latency traffic to fallback pool.

Maria (oncall): action plan (live): 1) pause prefix-hash rollout (rollback flag) 2) enable aggressive prefetch warm-up for top 1000 prefixes 3) divert 20% traffic to fallback routing pool (older hash) 4) notify CS. executing now.

Zach (runtime): rolling back rollout flag to v1 -> `curl -X POST https://ops/api/flags/prefix-hash -d '{"version":"v1"}'`  (running).

Jun (sre): increasing prefetch_warmup to 1000 keys for namespace A:```kube exec -it prefetcher -- /app/prefetch --namespace A --top 1000```

Leo (prod-ops): routing change applied: traffic split 80/20 stable/fallback. Monitoring for queue length and KV latency.

Maria (oncall): CS-Alex, any customer reports yet?

CS-Alex: we got 2 support tickets from a single midmarket customer reporting "slow streaming completions" starting ~08:05. They flagged degraded UX. I've told them we're investigating and will provide status in 30m.

Priya (eng-ml): small change: add temporary increased KV client parallelism to reduce single-key pressure: `KV_CLIENT_MAX_INFLIGHT=64` for prefetch worker group. Deploying.

SRE-bot: Detected p95 -> 560ms within 4 minutes of mitigations; p99 still ~2.1s. KV latency falling from 22ms -> 7ms.

Jun (sre): good. still seeing some streaming stall traces attributed to requests that hit cold misses before warmup finished. tail still elevated but trending down.

Zach (runtime): started a background bucket-warm for hot prefixes: job id warm-20260315-01. 

Maria (oncall): can we run a quick smoke on a few affected customers' tenant prefixes to validate warm?

Priya (eng-ml): running validation harness against customer prefix set; initial results: hit-rate for sampled prefixes jumped to 88% after warm job.

SRE-bot: monitoring: p95 480ms, p99 1.05s after 12 minutes. error rate normalized.

CS-Alex: updated customer with interim fix and ETA for full restoration. Customer is relieved but wants postmortem.

Maria (oncall): next steps for handoff: - keep rollout paused until follow-up validation - run full investigation into rollout gating for cache key compatibility - add automated prewarm step to rollout pipeline - prepare postmortem and customer-facing blameless summary.

Jun (sre): root cause hypothesis: prefix-hash v2 produced a different key derivation for some legacy client prefixes (edge-case salt ordering), which meant previously-warm cache entries were not discoverable -> massive cold miss wave -> increased backend IO and request queuing -> streaming stalls and p99 spikes.

Zach (runtime): immediate mitigations done. long term: add cross-version compatibility layer + migration tool to rehash existing cache entries when doing a key-scheme change.

Leo (prod-ops): ticketing: creating infra incident ticket INC-2026-2897 and linking deploy ids + releasenotes.

Maria (oncall): handoff: I'm going offline in 10m. Jun will own until incident is closed. Jun, please include the list of affected customers (from CS) in the incident ticket and schedule postmortem.

Jun (sre): ack. will maintain monitoring and update tonight's oncall. compiling quick timeline + artifact links: deploy id d-20260315-08:00, warm job warm-20260315-01, flag rollback event id f-2897654321.

Priya (eng-ml): for postmortem: I'll attach perf traces showing kv latencies, prefix hit-rate heatmap, and the exact diff in hash function.

Maria (oncall): thanks team. summary for next oncall: mitigations applied, majority of customer impact resolved, owning SRE: Jun, followups: prewarm + migration tooling + rollout gating. leaving thread. :thumbsup:

Jun (sre): final note: customers with persistent issues after warm should be routed to manual warm or tenant-specific fallback until migration is done. I'll update runbook accordingly.

SRE-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigated). p95/p99 back within SLO guardrails. Postmortem required.

CS-Alex: will follow up with customer NPS impact and coordinate comms.

Maria (oncall): closing handoff. full postmortem draft due EOD+2.

Jun (sre): adding action items to INC-2026-2897: ["add prewarm step to rollout", "compat check in CI for prefix hash changes", "migration tool to rehash cache entries", "customer comms + postmortem"]

Zach (runtime): will add compatibility check PR and link to incident.

CS-Alex: thanks all, keeping customer updated.

(React: many :white_check_mark: and :heart: across messages)
